facts.text: Wheel loaders and haul trucks are many times heavier than cars.
facts.quote: A wheel loader or haul truck is many times heavier than a car

facts.text: Wheel loaders and haul trucks have large blind spots.
facts.quote: has large blind spots

facts.text: Wheel loaders and haul trucks work in reverse much of the time.
facts.quote: works in reverse much of the time

facts.text: Wheel loaders and haul trucks share job sites with people on foot and light vehicles.
facts.quote: shares the site with people on foot and light vehicles

facts.text: The deadliest documented accident pattern is a large machine moving over a person or light vehicle that the operator cannot see.
facts.quote: The deadliest documented accident pattern is a large machine moving over a person or a light vehicle that the operator cannot see.

facts.text: Most heavy off-road machines already carry a warning system that beeps at the operator.
facts.quote: Most machines already carry a warning system that beeps at the operator.

facts.text: The Collision Mitigation System studied in the booklet brakes on its own rather than only warning the operator.
facts.quote: The system studied in the booklet goes one step further: it brakes on its own.

facts.text: In the mining industry's nine-level control model, warning is Level 8 and automatic intervention is Level 9.
facts.quote: In the mining industry's language, warning is "Level 8" and automatic intervention is "Level 9" of a nine-level control model.

facts.text: Engineering safety assessment asks what could go wrong, how severe and likely the consequences would be, and what evidence demonstrates sufficient risk reduction.
facts.quote: They ask "what could go wrong, how bad would it be, how likely is it, and what evidence shows we have reduced it enough?"

facts.text: A safety case organizes a safety claim, supporting arguments, and the evidence behind each argument.
facts.quote: The answers are organized into a safety case: a claim, the arguments that support it, and the evidence behind each argument.

facts.text: Standards such as ISO 21815 and ISO 19014 specify what safety arguments must cover.
facts.quote: Standards such as ISO 21815 and ISO 19014 say what the arguments must cover

facts.text: Laws such as the EU Machinery Regulation specify when safety evidence must exist.
facts.quote: laws such as the EU Machinery Regulation, which applies from January 2027, say when the evidence must exist.

facts.text: The EU Machinery Regulation applies from January 2027.
facts.quote: the EU Machinery Regulation, which applies from January 2027

facts.text: A braking system can only brake for objects its sensors detect.
facts.quote: A braking system can only brake for what its sensors detect.

facts.text: Cameras, lidar, radar and ultrasonic sensors perceive the world differently and have different failure behavior in dust, fog, snow, rain, darkness and glare.
facts.quote: Cameras, lidar, radar and ultrasonic sensors each see the world differently, and each fails differently in dust, fog, snow, rain, darkness and glare.

facts.text: Every detection system makes false-negative errors, such as missing a real person, and false-positive errors, such as reacting to something harmless.
facts.quote: Every detection system makes two kinds of mistake: it misses a real person (a false negative) or it reacts to something harmless (a false positive).

facts.text: Tuning a detection system to reduce misses increases false alarms.
facts.quote: Tuning it to make fewer misses makes more false alarms

facts.text: On a heavy machine with automatic braking, a false alarm can result in a brake slam.
facts.quote: on a heavy machine a false alarm is a brake slam.

facts.text: Operators switch off systems that brake for nothing.
facts.quote: Operators switch off systems that brake for nothing.

facts.text: Simulation allows teams to run millions of situations that would not be staged with a real worker, long before a prototype exists.
facts.quote: Simulation lets the team run millions of situations that nobody would stage with a real worker, long before the prototype exists.

facts.text: A simulation consists of models of the machine, ground, sensors, weather and people.
facts.quote: But a simulation is made of models: of the machine, the ground, the sensors, the weather and the people.

facts.text: Each simulation model must be compared with measurements before its answers can be trusted.
facts.quote: Each model must be compared with measurements before its answers can be trusted.

facts.text: Simulation does not replace physical tests; simulation identifies which physical tests merit scarce prototype time and multiplies the evidence around those tests.
facts.quote: simulation does not replace physical tests; it decides which physical tests are worth the scarce prototype time and multiplies the evidence around them.
